label: final copy step of length-3 sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost always on the last output step (to_go==0 holds 92% of mass). It is strongly specific to short sequences: L=3 final step (t=5, input = orig(1), output = orig(2)) carries ~71% of mass and fires on ~64% of such steps; L=4 final step (t=7) adds ~19% but fires on only ~7% of those steps, mostly when the input token is o, t or j. Strongest activations are L=3 final steps with input o, t, 3, m, j. Never fires in the original or delimiter phases, nor on the first occurrence of a token. Weak, sparse residual activations at the end of longer sequences (L>=5). The L=3 predicate misses the L=4 cases and ~36% of L=3 final steps are silent, so the description is incomplete.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: o, j, t, i, m, r; least: y, q, 0, k) and the input two steps back (most: n, a, j, c, k, y; least: s, x, 3, m); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=5, L=3, L=4 & t=7.
